lessonRef.subject: financial-literacy
lessonRef.title: Mastery check: unpaid family and community work

objective: Learners quantify invented unpaid community work in hours and translate it into a monetary value at a stated pretend rate.
scenario: Fern is a made-up fifth grader documenting a pretend community garden build. Three invented volunteers each work 6 hours, and the invented equivalent paid rate is $16.00 an hour. Materials cost $95.00. Nobody is actually paid.
safetyNotes: Every amount, person, business, and account in this task is invented for practice. Nothing here refers to a real household.
Never write a real bank account, card, PIN, password, Social Security, or tax number on this sheet; the task never asks for one.
This is education, not individualized financial advice. Real money decisions belong to a trusted adult.

tasks.directions: Total the invented volunteer hours: 3 people at 6 hours each.

prompts.text: How many volunteer hours went into the build?

tasks.directions: Put the invented $16.00 rate on those hours, then set that value beside the $95.00 actually spent on materials.

prompts.text: What would the 18 hours have cost at $16.00 an hour?
How much larger is the volunteer value than the material cost?

tasks.directions: A second invented work day adds 12 more volunteer hours and another $40.00 of materials.

prompts.text: What is the volunteer value across both days?
What did the whole project cost in money across both days?

tasks.directions: The receipts totalled far less than the work.

prompts.text: Fern's receipts show $135.00. Explain what that figure leaves out and why a community project can be undervalued by its accounts.

remediation: If a learner multiplies by volunteers instead of hours, compute Fern's hour total as its own boxed figure first, then apply the rate to that box.
extension: Ask the learner what other contributions Fern's hour count still misses, and how a project might record them.
